canonical_text: ADSCs also modulate the remaining arms of the immune system, though the clinical evidence is less extensive than for macrophages and T-cells. **B cells** are nudged toward a regulatory phenotype (Bregs) that produces the anti-inflammatory cytokine IL-10 and suppresses autoantibody production, with relevance to organ transplantation and autoimmune disease (Frontiers in Immunology, 2022; 2025). **Dendritic cells**, which capture antigens and present them to T-cells, have their maturation blocked by ADSC-secreted PGE2, IL-6, and IL-10, reducing their capacity to trigger an adaptive immune response (Djouad et al., *Blood*, 2009; Spaggiari et al., *Blood*, 2009). **Natural killer cells**, essential for cancer surveillance and viral defense, have their cytotoxicity reduced by TGF-beta and PGE2, which downregulate perforin and granzyme B expression; adipose-derived MSCs appear particularly effective at this compared to other MSC sources (Scientific Reports, 2021). **Neutrophils**, the first immune cells to arrive at any injury, have their excessive infiltration reduced by TSG-6, which blocks their migration through interaction with the CD44 receptor.
